name: cattle
why: A Brainfuck toolkit is a small, strange corner of esoteric language tooling worth an afternoon of poking.

brief.what_it_is: Cattle is a toolkit for the Brainfuck programming language, designed to be embedded in other applications. It lets a host application inspect and run Brainfuck programs. The host can swap in its own input and output routines so that the interaction between the host and the Brainfuck interpreter is handled by the host. The interpreter's behaviour can be changed through a configuration object, which the page says can make it compatible with most other Brainfuck compilers and interpreters.
brief.why_it_exists: The page gives no explicit problem statement. It frames Cattle as a library for giving any application the ability to run Brainfuck, with I/O that the host controls.
brief.how_it_works: Cattle is built on GObject and follows GNOME-stack API conventions. GObject Introspection means it can be called from languages such as Scheme, Python and JavaScript. The page does not describe the interpreter's internals.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no install steps, build instructions or runtime requirements. It says released versions are available from a releases section and that current development code is in a Git repository. An API reference is included in all release tarballs. The link URLs were not exposed in the fetched text, so only the homepage is listed under links.
brief.standout: Cattle is a library, not a standalone interpreter. Its I/O is pluggable, and its GObject base makes it callable from several languages through introspection, which is unusual for a Brainfuck implementation.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage shows no release dates, version numbers or commit history, so I could not judge whether the project is active.
brief.caveats: The homepage does not state a license, supported platforms, or a version. It contains no install commands. I did not follow the releases, Git or API reference links because their URLs were not present in the fetched text. The Brew description and the homepage agree on the basic purpose. The scout note's 'afternoon of poking' is a judgment, not something the source states.
quotes: Cattle is a toolkit for the Brainfuck programming language.
to make the interaction between the hosting application and the Brainfuck interpreter completely transparent, Cattle can be configured to use a custom set of I/O routines instead of the default ones.
Cattle is based on GObject, and its API should look familiar to anyone with some experience in the GNOME stack
